page: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4 shared vCPUs, 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, 16.0 GB of system memory yielding 4.0 GB per core, and 150 GB of local SSD storage. It also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 3812.16 and high single-threaded compression speeds, including 40.86 GB/sec in gzip and 16.93 GB/sec in bzip3. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall into the average tier, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 14889.36 and uncached large-block read bandwidth of 113.71 GB/sec. However, the PassMark memory score is relatively weak at 1711.85, indicating a potential bottleneck for memory-intensive operations.

This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and moderate database operations, supported by a Redis SET performance of 8.73 million operations per second. While its single-core capabilities are strong, the shared CPU allocation and lower memory benchmark scores suggest it is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded processing or large-scale LLM inference. Qualitatively, the server offers a balanced resource density for standard web applications and development environments where extreme multi-core throughput is not the primary requirement.
